% Regression: hard05_v2 — renders (O_L(M))_{(l_1..l_L),(r_1..r_L)}.
% T05 v2 — RMP arXiv:2011.12127, Eq. (Fig:MPDO-O_L): the MPO O_L(M)
% generated by the MPDO tensor M "by contracting the same tensors
% VERTICALLY on a ring of length L".
%
% Formula:  (O_L(M))_{(l_1..l_L),(r_1..r_L)}
%             = Tr[ M(l_1,r_1) M(l_2,r_2) ... M(l_L,r_L) ],
% where M(l,r) is M read as a matrix on its physical index pair, the
% trace runs over the chain of physical indices (the ring closure), and
% the virtual indices (l_j, r_j) of each site stay open — they are the
% physical legs of the MPO O_L.
%
% Declarative rendering: the grid's chain axis is horizontal, so the
% RMP's vertical ring is drawn rotated by 90 degrees (the paper rotates
% it to emphasize "contract the SAME tensor along the other index"; a
% `bond dir=vertical` key would recover that orientation — not yet in
% the grammar).  Content is identical:
%   * op-row chain of M       -> every box keeps two open legs
%                                (M's virtual indices, up/down here);
%   * \tndots                 -> the length-L ellipsis;
%   * periodic                -> the ring: the chain wire (M's physical
%                                index) closes around the outside.
\documentclass[varwidth=19cm, border=6pt]{standalone}
\usepackage{amsmath, amssymb}
\usepackage{tenkz}
\begin{document}
\[
  O_L(M) \;=\;
  \begin{tenkz}[physical=updown, periodic, tensor style=box]
    \tn{M} & \tndots & \tn{M}
  \end{tenkz}
\]
\end{document}
